title: Frequency control writes a decile mid that is not on the frequency entity's step
claim: On every heating state the compressor frequency write sends FrequencyMap's decile midpoint (23.5, 37.5, 51.5, 86.5 Hz) to a number entity whose step is 1 Hz, so the command lies off the entity's grid in 50 of 50 heating rows (10 states x 5 rigs).
mechanism: coordinator._command_frequency sends round(target, 1) from freq_control.FrequencyMap.recommend, whose candidates are hz_min + (decile + 0.5) * span / 10; nothing puts the value on the entity's 'step' attribute, while every set-point write goes through inputs.write_setpoint, which does (setpoint_step). Home Assistant's number.set_value validates min/max only, so the off-step value reaches the device integration, which rounds, truncates or refuses it.

evidence.unit: rows (rig x state) with a frequency write off the entity step
evidence.machine: box B11, Linux 6.18.44 x86_64, venv-ci CPython 3.14
evidence.contention_note: count; contention-immune (two other seats on the box)

perturbation.change: --perturb freq_grid: FrequencyMap.recommend's answer rounded to the entity's 1 Hz step (the one-line production edit: quantise the target on the entity step before set_value)

metric_definition: Rows (rig x enumerator state) where a number.set_value to the frequency entity carries a value not equal to round(v/step)*step or outside min..max (count key: the value the seam delivered).
phenomenon_property: Every number written to an actuator entity lies on that entity's own step and inside its min..max, whatever writer computes it.
seam_rule: grep -n '"set_value"\|services.async_call' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py  # every number write not routed through inputs.write_setpoint

null_control.note: the same rigs with the frequency entity stating a 0.5 Hz step: every decile mid is on it and clause_grid reads 0

proposed_fix_scope: coordinator._command_frequency: quantise the target onto the frequency entity's step (inputs.setpoint_step / _on_step) inside its range before the call and the dedup.
